chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

easyC.name: C major (Lauren's 'easy C' — 2-finger reduction)
easyC.note: Reduced 2-finger C voicing for confidence-building. Spelling verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as C E G. 'Lauren's easy C' is a teaching label; arithmetic proves the fingering spells C major and is playable.

pivot_points.static_finger: none — both fingers lift and re-land (different frets)
pivot_points.movement: Em middle(2)/ring(3) on A/D 2nd fret -> easyC ring(3) on A 3rd fret + middle(2) on D 2nd fret; index not yet used.

exercises.name: Make easy C
exercises.purpose: Land the 2-finger reduction (ring on A 3rd, middle on D 2nd).

params.fingers: ring(3) on A-string 3rd fret, middle(2) on D-string 2nd fret
params.open_strings: low E, G, B, high e all ring

exercises.coaching: Easy C is just two fingers, and we use this smaller version on purpose so it's not a fight. Ring on the A string third fret, middle on the D string second fret. The rest of the strings stay open and ring out by themselves. Same chord as the full C, just easier to land. You'll build up to the bigger version later.

exercises.name: Your first song — Em to easy C
exercises.purpose: Loop the two chords slowly; aim for no stopping.

params.cue: one strum per chord, then switch

exercises.coaching: Here's your song: E minor, strum. Easy C, strum. Back to E minor. Slow is fine — the goal is not stopping, not speed. Your fingers will fumble the change at first; that's normal, that's exactly what the loop is for. You are literally playing a song right now.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: I grin because this is the good part — the part most apps make you wait weeks for. 'Two chords and you can play a song. No joke. Today you'll learn an easy version of C, then we loop it with the E minor you already know. That loop? That's a song. You're about to play one.'
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: Easy C is just two fingers, and here's the trick — we're using a smaller version so it's not a fight. Ring finger on the A string, third fret. Middle finger on the D string, second fret. Everything else stays open and rings out on its own. Easier than the full C, same chord, and you'll upgrade later. For now, this is your C.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Now the fun bit. Loop it: E minor, strum. Easy C, strum. Back to E minor. Slow's fine — the win isn't speed, it's not stopping between them. Your fingers will fumble the first few times. That's normal, that's the whole point of looping. You just played a song. Go tell somebody.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can go E minor to easy C to E minor without a full stop, you played a song. That's the hook that keeps people coming back — protect it. It won't be smooth yet, and it's not supposed to be.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Two chords, one loop, a real song. Most apps make you wait weeks for this — you got it in lesson three. Practice the loop a little every day. Lesson four adds the rhythm, and then it really sounds like music. See you there.
